record.title: Embodied First Exam brings coding-agent evaluation to diverse simulated robots
record.summary: A Nov. 9 arXiv preprint introduces the Embodied First Exam (EFE), a framework that lets coding agents choose direct control, code-generated control, or policy training across 1,156 tasks in 35 suites and 47 simulated robots. It separates sensor-only Standard and Realtime settings from a Privileged setting with full simulator state and unlimited resets. On 391 core tasks with paired Privileged and Standard tests, the authors report GPT-6 Astra in Codex solved 77% in Privileged and 30% in Standard; adding resets to the Standard interface raised success to 53%, while adding both resets and exact object state raised it to 68%. These are preprint-reported simulation results, not independently reproduced physical-robot capability measurements.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors introduce EFE with 1,156 tasks in 35 suites spanning 47 robots, including 9 new suites, and define Privileged, Standard and Realtime evaluation settings.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across 391 paired core tasks, the paper reports GPT-6 Astra in Codex success of 77% in Privileged and 30% in Standard; controlled additions of resets and exact state raise Standard success to 53% and 68%, respectively.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The paper was posted to arXiv on November 9, 2026.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected sources do not establish independent reproduction, repeated-attempt reliability, or robust performance on physical robots; all scored results in the paper are simulated.

evidence_gaps.description: The task suite, exact harness/model versions and leaderboard results were not independently replayed in this activation.
The authors note the hard core set excluded tasks initially solved by GPT-6 Luna, a model in the GPT-6 family. The effect of this filter on cross-agent comparisons is unmeasured.
Aggregate results are simulation-only; the small real-robot demonstration is excluded from reported scores.

brief.importance_rationale: If adopted and validated, an agent-native benchmark spanning 47 robot embodiments could change how general-purpose coding agents are evaluated for robotics. The reported scores remain simulation-based and paper-reported, so this is a measurement contribution rather than evidence of reliable physical-robot autonomy.
limitations: The benchmark paper and all scores are author-reported and were not independently reproduced here.
The core set was selected partly using GPT-6 Luna screening, which may bias comparisons involving the GPT-6 family.
Single attempts per agent-test pair do not establish reliability under repeated runs.
Simulation results and a small excluded physical demonstration do not establish general physical-robot capability.
brief.summary: A Nov. 9 arXiv preprint introduces the Embodied First Exam (EFE), a framework that lets coding agents choose direct control, code-generated control, or policy training across 1,156 tasks in 35 suites and 47 simulated robots. It separates sensor-only Standard and Realtime settings from a Privileged setting with full simulator state and unlimited resets. On 391 core tasks with paired Privileged and Standard tests, the authors report GPT-6 Astra in Codex solved 77% in Privileged and 30% in Standard; adding resets to the Standard interface raised success to 53%, while adding both resets and exact object state raised it to 68%. These are preprint-reported simulation results, not independently reproduced physical-robot capability measurements.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report the task-suite scope and model results, including 77% Privileged versus 30% Standard success for GPT-6 Astra in Codex over 391 paired tasks.
technical.demonstrated_result: A dated arXiv preprint is publicly available; this establishes publication of the paper, not the reported robot-agent success rates.
technical.mechanism: An agent receives a natural-language goal and may select direct action output, write a controller/program, or train a policy. The benchmark fixes initial scenes, resource budgets and external success verifiers while varying state visibility, reset access and whether the world continues during reasoning.
technical.regime: Eight model-harness combinations evaluated on a selected 456-task hard core set; paired setting analysis covers 391 tasks. Each agent makes one attempt per test. All reported scores are from simulation.
technical.strongest_baseline: Within-task paired comparisons contrast the same agent on Privileged and Standard settings. The paper reports GPT-6 Astra in Codex at 77% versus 30% on 391 paired core tasks; resetting and exact-state ablations partially close the gap.

brief.title: Embodied First Exam brings coding-agent evaluation to diverse simulated robots
brief.why_it_matters: EFE makes state access, reset availability and real-time pressure explicit evaluation variables for general-purpose coding agents controlling robots. Its paired results suggest that success under privileged simulation can substantially overstate performance under sensor-limited, less reversible conditions. The framework may help separate planning and control failures across robot types, while its selected core set and simulation-only evidence limit what the scores establish.
